## Summary

Nuclear geometry can exhibit fluctuations beyond a fixed average deformation, including
shape coexistence between competing nuclear configurations. This poster investigated how
such shape fluctuations influence the initial geometry of high-energy heavy-ion
collisions.

Using a Glauber Monte Carlo model, the study examined the effect of nuclear shape
coexistence on observables including eccentricity and transverse-area fluctuations. The
results demonstrated that multiparticle correlations in heavy-ion collisions can retain
sensitivity to fluctuations of the underlying nuclear shape.
